name: Closing the loop: action callback, SDK, self-health, end-to-end adapter canary
intro: Four items shipped together, each closing a previously-loose end: the inbound action-callback edge (Truehound can finally learn what happened to an action it proposed), the @truehound/sdk customer package (typed BFF client + HMAC verifier + signer), /status page surfacing operational substrate (outbound fanout, drift, Pulse), and a PagerDuty end-to-end canary test that pins the full chain (spec → client → drift detector → outbound emit) with realistic vendor JSON. Together they turn Truehound from open-loop dashboard into closed control plane with customer-facing SDK and self-health visibility. 864 BFF + 75 MCP + 271 CLI + 7,310 SPA + 17 SDK tests, all green.

bullets.label: POST /api/v1/actions/{id}/callback
bullets.detail: The state machine in audit-replay.js already knew about action.executed / action.failed; nothing wired the lifecycle from outside. Now: per-action HMAC auth (each action gets a unique callback_secret minted at propose time, returned once in the actions/batch response), state machine approved → executed | failed, idempotent on deliveryId. Two audit rows (action.callback_received + terminal) + outbound fan-out of the terminal event.

bullets.label: 21 unit tests + OpenAPI path schema
bullets.detail: Covers signature verification, body validation, state-machine transitions, idempotent replay returns prior outcome unchanged, all four error codes (action_not_found, state_invalid, unauthorized, invalid_*). docs/specs/OUTBOUND_WEBHOOKS.md updated with §6 documenting the inbound contract.

bullets.label: AtlasClient + webhook helpers
bullets.detail: Customers integrating against Truehound wrote raw fetch + their own HMAC + their own retry. The new SDK package wraps the BFF API with typed methods (subscription lifecycle, propose-action-batch, send-action-callback) + verifyOutboundWebhook helper for the subscriber side + signActionCallback for the executor side. AtlasApiError carries the typed code so callers switch exhaustively against bff/src/error-codes.js.

bullets.label: Honest defaults
bullets.detail: Per-request AbortController + configurable timeoutMs (default 10s). sendActionCallback skips bearer auth because the HMAC IS the credential. ESM with declaration-only TS emit; same package pattern as backstage-plugin. 17 tests covering signing roundtrip, every verification edge case, header injection, and a full propose → callback roundtrip.

bullets.label: Three traffic-light rows next to the seeded infra components
bullets.detail: Outbound webhook fanout (localStorage subs + shared subscriptionHealth.ts classifier — band counts collapse to operational/degraded/outage); drift detection (open high-or-critical findings from useDriftRecords); Pulse signals (persistent high-or-critical signals). Surfaces "is Truehound itself healthy" alongside the customer-facing uptime page.

bullets.label: Pure derivations, tested
bullets.detail: src/data/truth/operationalSubstrate.ts holds the four helpers. Each takes plain inputs (not React Query results) so the 14 vitest cases don't have to mock the query layer. Covers every band transition and the edge cases (null storage, unknown severities, ok=true with non-empty failures).

bullets.label: The full chain crossed in one test
bullets.detail: Unit tests covered each layer individually. Nothing crossed all five layers (spec → createVendorClient → drift detector → vendor-backed rules → outbound emit) with a single realistic vendor JSON shape. New bff/src/vendors/pagerduty-e2e.test.js mocks only the HTTP boundary; every layer above is real.

bullets.label: Wire format + chain + degradation
bullets.detail: Three wire-format tests pin the URL, auth header, and JSON normalisation. Four chain tests pin: incident.unmitigated_critical fires + emits, negative case (resolved incident) pinned, schedule.no_rotation fires for tier-1, a 401 from PagerDuty degrades gracefully. If a refactor breaks the chain, this fails first.

name: Outbound loop + agent/operator surface: subscription lifecycle, drift fanout, agent-discoverable rules
intro: A 24-hour arc focused on a single product story: close the loop between Truehound detecting something and the customer's tools learning about it. Drift the detector finds now fans out through outbound webhooks; subscription lifecycle is end-to-end (PATCH / replay / reactivate / rotate-secret / deliveries + admin health roll-up); five new operational-signal drift rules + one adapter-freshness drift rule give the detector real coverage; the drift-rule registry is now reachable by agents through a new MCP tool; operators get a first-class CLI subcommand for outbound-webhook health. 836 BFF + 73 MCP + 271 CLI + 7,284 SPA tests all green.

sections.title: Drift fanout closes the customer loop

bullets.label: drift.detected outbound delivery
bullets.detail: The detector's docstring claimed it; the reality was audit-only until this arc. Drift findings now emit through the existing outbound-webhook substrate, so a Slack/PagerDuty/custom subscriber learns about a new finding the moment Truehound does. Wired via an emit callback threaded through detectDriftForTenant — the detector stays pure, the route owns the delivery contract.

bullets.label: Five new operational-signal drift rules
bullets.detail: monitor.firing_alert, slo.budget_exhausting, incident.unmitigated_critical, schedule.no_rotation, vulnerability.backlog_high. Ported from xcl governance rules; each runs through the same vendor-backed registry as the prior 6 (skipped silently when no vendor client is connected). Drift rule count: 13 → 18 intrinsic + 1 adapter scope.

bullets.label: adapter.stale_sync drift rule + sync tracker
bullets.detail: The freshness contract was a doc claim until this arc. Every webhook ingest now records (tenant, adapter, kind, ts) through adapter-sync-tracker.js; the new adapter-scope drift rule emits medium/high findings when a configured adapter goes past 1× / 2× its staleAfterSec. Datadog / PagerDuty / Rootly / FireHydrant / ServiceNow / Compass have freshness budgets registered.

bullets.label: PATCH /api/v1/subscriptions/:id
bullets.detail: Update events + URL with SSRF re-check on the new URL — the create-time guard isn't bypassable via update.

bullets.label: POST /api/v1/subscriptions/:id/reactivate + rotate-secret
bullets.detail: Bring a subscription out of auto-deactivated state; rotate the HMAC secret without recreating the subscription (preserves event filter + delivery history).

bullets.label: POST /api/v1/subscriptions/:id/replay
bullets.detail: Replay a single DLQ row with the same deliveryId semantics — consumers idempotent on deliveryId won't double-process. Surfaces failure directly to the operator instead of routing through the retry ladder; replay is operator-driven, not automated.

bullets.label: GET /api/v1/subscriptions/:id/deliveries
bullets.detail: Subscriber-facing recent-delivery + DLQ view so a customer can self-serve health diagnostics without an admin-token call.

bullets.label: GET /api/v1/admin/subscriptions/health
bullets.detail: Admin roll-up: every subscription bucketed into failing / degraded / healthy bands via consecutiveFailures + DLQ depth + last-status. Sorted worst-first, deepest-DLQ first within band, secrets stripped. The one call an operator runs to see what's silently dropping events.

bullets.label: MCP tool: list_drift_rules
bullets.detail: Agents could ask drift_for_service "what drift is on this service?" but had no way to ask "what rules does Truehound actually run?". They needed it to reason about whether a clean drift response was real or rule-not-implemented. Returns the 19-row registry with { id, sources, vendorBacked, scope }, optional scope filter, demo-mode catalog kept in sync with BFF source. Tool count 16 → 17.

bullets.label: CLI: atlas subscriptions-health
bullets.detail: Operator counterpart to the admin endpoint. Worst-first markdown for paste-into-ticket, JSON for jq pipelines, secrets stripped end-to-end. --fail-on-failing exits 1 when totals.failing > 0 so a CI step can hard-fail when any subscriber is dropping events.

bullets.label: BFF: team-resolution-evidence endpoint
bullets.detail: The multi-source weighted-vote canonicalization result is now a first-class API surface — service → { canonical, sources, weights, ties }. Same code path the catalog ingest uses; the API lets a customer answer "why does Truehound think team X owns this service?" without scraping logs.

bullets.label: Per-vendor upstream budget + circuit breaker
bullets.detail: createUpstreamBudget({ defaults, overrides, now }) enforces a sliding-window per-vendor request budget; throws BudgetExceededError with retryAfterMs so callers can shed load cleanly. Pairs with a half-open probe so a vendor that recovers doesn't sit in breaker hell.

bullets.label: Response-cache wrapper with singleflight
bullets.detail: wrapWithResponseCache(cache, handler, opts) deduplicates concurrent identical requests via an inFlight Map — thundering herds against the same vendor endpoint collapse to one upstream call.

bullets.label: Error-code registry: 31 top-level + 9 field codes
bullets.detail: Every code returned by a BFF route is now in bff/src/error-codes.js. Contract test greps source for error: { code: "..." } literals and asserts every one is registered. Drift on either side is a CI failure.

bullets.label: Audit-kind registry: 27 kinds
bullets.detail: Every appendAudit kind frozen in bff/src/audit-kinds.js. Contract test walks every appendAudit(..., "<kind>", ...) call in source and asserts the kind is registered.

name: Calmation pass: enterprise-realistic seed + editorial visuals + in-browser chain verifiers
intro: A demo-quality pass that takes Truehound from competent dashboard to confident enterprise control plane. Two threads ran together: sample data across the full catalog is now weighted to enterprise reality instead of uniform 25% (Tenant Health 47 AT RISK → 70 HEALTHY, DORA scorecard 18 burning teams → 0, vulnerabilities 12 critical → 1, global Active-Signals 51 critical → 3-5), and the visual system switched to an editorial register (Fraunces display serif at 28-34px, severity chips by-dot-not-by-band, destructive red desaturated globally so its scarcity carries meaning).

bullets.label: VerifyChainButton on /audit
bullets.detail: Recomputes the 100-event SHA-256 chain via Web Crypto and surfaces "Chain verified · N events · Xms" in a green pill. Same canonical-JSON + SHA-256 the BFF uses; no round-trip, no trust assumption beyond what's already running in the browser.

bullets.label: TrustVerifyChainButton on /trust
bullets.detail: Runs the rich truth-layer verifier (hash / prevHash / seq link-walk) on the actions audit chain. Graceful "Nothing to verify yet · seal events first" state when the demo chain isn't sealed — accurate, not alarming.

bullets.label: ReceiptChip on /automation OutcomePane
bullets.detail: Click a freshly issued receipt to recompute records_hash + outcome_hash via verifyReceipt. Determinism receipt verifiable in 5ms client-side.

bullets.label: PageHeader uses Fraunces display serif
bullets.detail: 28-34px title, 13px relaxed-leading subtitle, mono-tracked breadcrumbs, no horizontal divider. Welcome + login screens get the same brand treatment. Propagates across all 75 routes without per-page edits.

bullets.label: Severity chips: dot + label, tone by severity not band
bullets.detail: WorkItemSeverity + PulseSignalSeverity rewritten — "TOP OF QUEUE · CRITICAL · 3d old" became a single Critical dot. When every visible row is top of queue by construction, repeating it on each chip is noise.

bullets.label: Desaturated destructive + amber-shifted bands
bullets.detail: --destructive chroma 0.22 → 0.175. "In trouble" / "weak" bands shifted to amber; crisis stays destructive (rare). Reserves red for actions the operator can reject or undo.

bullets.label: EmptyState rebuilt
bullets.detail: h-14 rounded-2xl icon container with soft radial halo, Fraunces title, 16px breathing room. Reads as confident "nothing to do" instead of "page failed."

sections.title: Sample data calibrated to enterprise reality

bullets.label: Severity distributions weighted (was uniform 25%)
bullets.detail: Violations 5/20/35/40, incidents 6/16/36/42, releases 92/5/3 succeed/failed/rolled-back, vulnerabilities 6/16/36/42 + KEV 15%, alerts 5/13/32/50, monitors P1-P5 5/15/30/30/20, pulse signals weighted per category. Status outages dropped to ~1% per component.

bullets.label: Volume thresholds re-tuned
bullets.detail: Incident storm ≥25/week (was ≥8), drift surge ≥20/week (was ≥8), CFR band requires ≥5 deploys (no more "BURNING 100% · 1 deploy 1 failed"). Tier-1 SLO coverage 95% (was 60%). Ownership freshness 90% (was 78%). Dependency cycle max size 12-15 (was 242).

bullets.label: Tenant Health 47 → 70
bullets.detail: Customer Health computation now sees the full catalog (page-size cap raised). Composite reads HEALTHY at 70/100 with COVERAGE 79.

bullets.label: traceparent W3C middleware
bullets.detail: Strict v00 parser + Hono middleware; existing tracingMiddleware adopts inbound trace IDs so partner systems / agent chains see one continuous trace across the wire.

bullets.label: Cost-anomaly detector (MAD-z)
bullets.detail: Robust z-score for individual plan runs vs baseline. Wired into persistOutcome — when ≥5 prior runs of the same plan exist, anomalies (minor/major/extreme) land on the row + audit metadata.

bullets.label: Saved Views per-page filter persistence
bullets.detail: Picker + create modal + storage shape mirroring a production BFF. Wired into /catalog SQL playground; same component drops into other pages with a different page_key.

bullets.detail: Pagination cap was silently truncating the displayed catalog by a third.

bullets.label: DuckDB "Table services already exists" race
bullets.detail: CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE replaces the DROP+CREATE pair that was racing in React 18 strict mode under the shared DuckDB singleton.

bullets.label: ComposeAsk drawer first-paint bleed
bullets.detail: Switched from CSS-translate hide to mount-on-open. Tailwind 4's translate-x-* writes the new CSS translate property which was leaving the panel bleeding onto Inbox first-paint at 1440px.

bullets.detail: React Router was carrying a dead redirect that would surface a false 404 if matching ever reordered.

bullets.label: BFF: 728 → 749 tests (+21)
bullets.detail: traceparent + cost-anomaly + audit-route ports.

bullets.label: SPA: 7261 → 7277 tests (+16)
bullets.detail: Saved Views + audit verifier + new replay coverage.

name: v334 — DriftTriageQueueCard on /health — priority pill + 3-input tone-coded trace
intro: Visible payoff for v333. Slotted on /health directly below v332's team-scorecard card. /health carries 53 readiness cards. Distinguishing element: per-row priority pill + 3-input tone-coded trace (severity + age + disagreement chips, each tone-coded independently). Reader sees the triage answer AND the reasoning chain in one row — 'critical from severity' reads differently from 'critical escalated by age 22d', same priority, different story. 135th paired substrate → UI ship.

sections.title: Distinguishing element — priority + reasoning in one row

bullets.label: Priority pill (large solid block) + 3-input tone-coded trace
bullets.detail: Severity chip + age chip + disagree/agree chip each tinted by THEIR threshold. Reader sees which rule fired without reading the substrate's docstring. severity destructive + age muted + disagree → 'true critical'; severity warning + age destructive + agree → 'escalated by age'.

bullets.label: Age chip uses substrate's exact thresholds
bullets.detail: ≥ AGE_CRITICAL_DAYS (21d) → destructive; ≥ AGE_HIGH_DAYS (10d) → warning; else muted. Borrowed verbatim from xcl-tools opexDisputesQueue priority-computation thresholds.

bullets.label: ShieldAlert glyph tinted to topPriority
bullets.detail: Destructive on any critical / softer destructive on any high / warning on any medium / muted on low-only / success when empty. Absence of red is itself the leadership read.

bullets.label: 4 always-render priority chips with counts
bullets.detail: critical/high/medium/low always render — level-toned > 0, muted at zero. The shape of the four chips IS the queue posture.

bullets.label: Surfaces when DriftRecord has a proposedAction
bullets.detail: Right-edge primary-tinted chip tells the reviewer they can resolve this drift without writing the action from scratch. Hidden when no proposal exists.

bullets.label: 17 new component tests
bullets.detail: Skeleton; triage · priority badge; 4 priority chips with counts; oldest-Nd chip; oldest hidden when no drift; quiet state; row with pill + entity + team + severity + age + disagree; agree chip when no disagreement; critical row destructive border + pill; medium warning; low neutral; age chip ≥ 21d destructive / ≥ 10d warning; action-ready chip surfacing; action-ready hidden without title; topN plural overflow; singular when 1 left; builds rollup from input prop.

bullets.label: 4,121 SPA tests total (+17 vs v333)
bullets.detail: typecheck green; lint green; build green.

name: v333 — drift triage queue — priority-from-(severity × age × evidence) borrowed from xcl-tools opexDisputesQueue — 130th MCP tool
intro: Substrate ship. BORROWED — priority-from-(exposure × age × evidence) + 4-bucket priority ladder + typo-safe sortBy whitelist + age-driven escalation thresholds (AGE_CRITICAL_DAYS=21, AGE_HIGH_DAYS=10) from xcl-tools-bff opexDisputesQueue. Source ranks ownership disputes by (ARR × age × evidence). Truehound adapts: maps ARR → severity, evidence-count → source-disagreement bool, keeps age axis identical. Rule order is load-bearing — first-match-wins. Distinct from driftByTeam (count rollup, no priority) and driftDiscoveryTrendByWeek (temporal, no priority): v333 is the per-record triage that answers 'attack this drift first.' MCP catalog grows 129 → 130.

bullets.label: 4-bucket priority ladder (critical/high/medium/low)
bullets.detail: Source repo's contract preserved. Each bucket carries its own tone signature downstream (UI + MCP).

bullets.label: Age thresholds: 21d critical, 10d high
bullets.detail: Lifted directly from source's AGE_CRITICAL_DAYS / AGE_HIGH_DAYS. Truehound applies them to firstSeenAt instead of dispute raised_ts — same semantics.

bullets.label: Typo-safe sortBy whitelist
bullets.detail: Unknown values fall through to default (priority). Source: 'a typo in the FE query doesn't crash the request.'

bullets.label: Rule order is load-bearing (first-match-wins)
bullets.detail: A medium-severity drift open for 22d wins critical, not medium, because the age rule fires first. Truehound keeps the source's `if … return; if … return;` ordering intact.

bullets.label: ARR exposure → severity rank
bullets.detail: Source repo's ARR-tier thresholds become Truehound's severity union (critical/high/medium/low). The semantic 'how much business is at stake' question maps cleanly across.

bullets.label: Conflicting-evidence-count → sourceDisagreement (bool)
bullets.detail: Truehound's DriftRecord has exactly 2 sources (a + b) — disagreement is binary, not a count. Substrate detects sources.a.value !== sources.b.value.

bullets.label: Service-kind affected entity resolves team from services list
bullets.detail: Authoritative service.team lookup — gives the row a 'who needs to act?' answer without overloading the affected-entity name field.

bullets.label: 36 new substrate tests
bullets.detail: Constants borrowed verbatim; computeDriftPriority rule-order truth table (14 cases — including critical-severity short-circuit, age boundaries at 9/10 and 20/21 days, source disagreement gates, severity floors); build (22 cases — empty; source disagreement detection; future-date clamp; service team resolution; non-service unowned; unknown-service unowned; byPriority counts all 4 buckets; topPriority = highest non-empty; oldestDriftAgeDays tracks max; default sort by priority → ageDays → id; sortBy overrides ageDays/severity/affectedTeam; unknown sortBy → default; proposedActionTitle surfaced; invalid firstSeenAt excluded; generatedAt).

bullets.label: 4,104 SPA tests total (+36 vs v332)
bullets.detail: typecheck green; lint green; build green. MCP catalog grows 129 → 130.

name: v332 — TeamScorecardCard on /health — letter-grade tile + 5-metric stat strip
intro: Visible payoff for v331. Slotted on /health directly below v330's action-throughput card. /health carries 52 readiness cards. Distinguishing element: per-row large letter-grade tile (32px A/B/C/D, color-coded) + 5-metric stat strip where each stat carries its own threshold tone. Grade is the primary affordance — scan down for leadership read, across for details. 134th paired substrate → UI ship.

sections.title: Distinguishing element — letter-grade tile + 5-metric stat strip

bullets.label: Large 32px grade tile color-coded A/B/C/D
bullets.detail: A success-deep; B success-muted; C warning; D destructive. Tile is the primary visual cue — leaders see grade distribution at a glance before reading any numbers.

bullets.label: 5-metric stat strip with independent threshold tones
bullets.detail: inc 30d (≥15 destructive / ≥5 warning), open (≥3 / ≥1), mttr (≥120m / ≥60m), unowned (≥2 / ≥1), runbook (<50% / <80%). A muted strip + A tile = healthy; destructive strip + D tile = team in trouble.

bullets.label: GraduationCap glyph tinted to worst grade present
bullets.detail: Destructive on any D; warning on any C; success otherwise. Absence of red is itself the leadership read.

bullets.label: 4 always-render grade chips + 'worst <team>' callout
bullets.detail: D / C / B / A always show, level-toned > 0, muted at zero. Worst-team chip surfaces the highest-penalty team for one-click triage.

bullets.label: D destructive / C warning / A&B neutral
bullets.detail: Border matches the tile so the row reads as one band of urgency.

bullets.label: 14 new component tests
bullets.detail: Skeleton; grade · 30d badge; 4 grade chips (verifies '1 team' singular vs 'N teams' plural grammar); worst-team callout; quiet state; full row (grade tile + team + service count + score + 5 stats); D destructive border + tile; C warning border + tile; A/B success tiles + neutral border; MTTR null em-dash; MTTR format 30m vs 3.0h; topN plural overflow; singular overflow when 1 left; builds rollup from input prop.

bullets.label: 4,068 SPA tests total (+14 vs v331)
bullets.detail: typecheck green; lint green; build green.

name: v331 — team scorecard — A/B/C/D composite + higher-is-worse sort borrowed from xcl-tools opexTeamScorecard — 129th MCP tool
intro: Substrate ship. BORROWED — A/B/C/D letter-grade composite + higher-is-worse / higher-is-better sort convention + typo-safe sortBy whitelist from xcl-tools-bff opexTeamScorecard. Source maps 7 metrics → A/B/C/D over an 8-team fixture; Truehound adapts to per-team operational scorecard derived LIVE from substrate. Penalty score weights: 0.30 incidents + 0.25 open + 0.20 mttr + 0.15 unowned + 0.10 runbook-gap, each clip01-bounded. Grade: ≤24 A, ≤49 B, ≤74 C, else D. MCP catalog grows 128 → 129.

bullets.label: A/B/C/D 4-letter scale
bullets.detail: Source's letter grade contract. Truehound re-derives the value from a different metric set but keeps the 4-bucket shape so downstream consumers (UI + agent) work unchanged.

bullets.label: Higher-is-worse / higher-is-better sort convention
bullets.detail: incidents / MTTR / open / unowned sort DESC (worst floats up); runbook coverage sorts ASC (worst floats up). Both directions land the worst case at the top — borrowed verbatim from source's 'worst floats to top' invariant.

bullets.label: Typo-safe sortBy whitelist
bullets.detail: Unknown sortBy values fall through to the default ('grade'). Source repo: 'a typo in the FE query doesn't crash the request.' Truehound preserves the convention.

bullets.label: 5-axis weighted sum, each clip01-bounded
bullets.detail: incidents 30%, open 25%, mttr 20%, unowned 15%, runbook-gap 10%. Caps: 20 incidents / 5 open / 120m MTTR / 3 unowned / 0% runbook. Each axis saturates independently so a single runaway metric can't dominate.

bullets.label: Null MTTR + null runbook coverage = 0 contribution
bullets.detail: Quiet teams with no resolved incidents (null mttr) and teams with no services (null runbook) don't get penalized for missing data. Defensive against false-bad readings on data-quality gaps.

bullets.label: 33 new substrate tests
bullets.detail: Sortable-fields whitelist; classifyGrade boundary at every threshold + out-of-range clip; computePenaltyScore per-axis saturation + nulls + all-saturated; build (empty; one quiet team → A; window-bounded incidents30d; open + monitoring count as open; MTTR mean over resolved-in-window; MTTR null on 0; unowned via empty/placeholder/malformed; runbook coverage math; default sort grade DESC; sortBy override; runbookCoverage sorts ASC (worst first); team sorts alpha; unknown sortBy falls through; gradeCounts sums to total; services without team → unowned; future-dated excluded; orphan-incidents excluded; generatedAt).

bullets.label: 4,054 SPA tests total (+33 vs v330)
bullets.detail: typecheck green; lint green; build green. MCP catalog grows 128 → 129.

name: v330 — ActionThroughputCard on /health — paired velocity bars + 24h spike chip + top-stale list
intro: Visible payoff for v329. Slotted on /health directly below v328's fix-verification card. /health carries 51 readiness cards. Distinguishing element: per-row paired velocity bars — LEFT bar (destructive) = proposedInWindow, RIGHT bar (success) = executedInWindow, both scaled to maxSide across surfaced rows. Reader sees rate of intake AND rate of clearance in one glance. Border tone ladder + fleet headline glyph all tinted by netThroughput. 133rd paired substrate → UI ship.

bullets.label: Two narrow tracks side-by-side, sharing a common scale
bullets.detail: LEFT bar = proposed-in-window (destructive-tinted), RIGHT bar = executed-in-window (success-tinted). Count labels flank each bar so 4P · 1X reads as 'proposed 4 vs executed 1.' Left longer than right = team taking on actions faster than clearing them.

bullets.label: Common scale (maxSide across surfaced rows)
bullets.detail: Bars sized against the highest single-side count, so the eye can compare team-A's velocity to team-B's at a glance — not just within a row but across rows.

bullets.label: 24h slice is ALWAYS the last 24h, regardless of windowDays
bullets.detail: Source repo's load-bearing invariant: 'a sliding window confuses the is-this-a-spike-right-now question.' Truehound preserves it — the spike chip is independent of the window picker so a wave of proposals never gets averaged out by a wider trend window.

bullets.label: 24h NP · NX format
bullets.detail: Compact: 24h 5P · 3X reads as 'last day: 5 proposed, 3 executed.' Tooltip surfaces the full count.

sections.title: Net throughput sign convention (INVERTED from source)

bullets.label: Source: net > 0 = graph growing. Truehound: net > 0 = backlog SHRINKING.
bullets.detail: The semantics flip because actions are the opposite of edges — we WANT them executed, not accumulated. Substrate's netThroughput = executedInWindow - proposedInWindow. Positive = clearing faster than adding (good); negative = backlog growing (bad).

bullets.label: Tone ladder follows the inversion
bullets.detail: Headline glyph + net chip + row border all paint success on positive net, destructive on net ≤ -3, warning on -1 / -2, muted on 0.

bullets.label: Compact 'Top stale actions' panel below the team rows
bullets.detail: Surfaces the longest-waiting actions fleet-wide (oldest first, capped at 5 by default). Each entry shows age-tinted pill + target id + team + status. Provides the 'what specifically is stuck?' read that the per-team aggregate hides.

bullets.label: 18 new component tests
bullets.detail: Skeleton; actions · 7d badge; 24h NP·NX spike chip; net chip 3-tone (success/destructive/muted); oldest chip 3-tier age tone; oldest hidden when no opens; quiet state copy; row carries rank + name + open + net + bars; paired-bar geometry (100%/50% example); row border tone ladder; per-row stale chip ≥7d / hidden <7d; Top stale list with target+age; topN plural overflow; singular overflow when 1 left; builds rollup from input prop.

bullets.label: 4,021 SPA tests total (+18 vs v329)
bullets.detail: typecheck green; lint green; build green.

name: v329 — action throughput — 24h spike + windowed net-change + top-N stale borrowed from xcl-tools opexServiceGraph.churn — 128th MCP tool
intro: Substrate ship. BORROWED — 24h-fixed spike slice + windowed net-change + top-N rollup from xcl-tools-bff opexServiceGraph.churn (getChurnSummary). Source answers 'is the graph spiking now AND what's the trend over the week?' Truehound adapts to corrective-action throughput: every action progresses through proposed → terminal. Net throughput per team = executed - proposed (positive = backlog shrinking). 24h slice fixed regardless of window (spike-detector invariant). MCP catalog grows 127 → 128.

bullets.label: 24h slice is the LAST 24h, regardless of windowDays
bullets.detail: Source repo's spike-detector invariant: a sliding window would average out a wave that just landed. Borrowed verbatim — the 24h numbers stay fixed even if the caller queries a 30-day trend.

bullets.label: windowDays clipped [1, 30] with saturation semantics
bullets.detail: Wider queries become the cap, not an error. Borrowed verbatim from source's CHURN_WINDOW_MAX_DAYS handling.

bullets.label: Top-N stale rollup (default 5, clipped [1, 50])
bullets.detail: Same shape as source's top_added / top_removed lists — actionable subset of the queue, capped for UI ergonomics.

bullets.label: v305 = current state; v329 = rate of change
bullets.detail: v305 asks 'how big is the postmortem-action-item backlog right now?' v329 asks 'how fast is the team clearing vs taking on actions?' Both compose: v305 shows where backlog sits, v329 shows whether the team is shrinking or growing it.

bullets.label: 'added' = proposedAt; 'removed' = execution.startedAt on terminal status

bullets.label: deltaPct = (verified - regressed) / regressed * 100; null when no baseline
bullets.detail: Source's gtm.fix_verification formula. Negative = fixing faster than regressing. Explicit null beats NaN — borrowed verbatim.

bullets.label: regressed: recurrence detected (regardless of item state)
bullets.detail: Most urgent signal — the fingerprint came back. Even if items aren't 100% done, the postmortem failed at its job.

bullets.label: unverified: partial completion + past follow-through window
bullets.detail: Past the deadline with items still open — the team won't get to it. Audit-list candidate.

bullets.label: inconclusive: partial completion + inside the window

bullets.label: Days-spanned chip beside the bar
bullets.detail: Reader sees the bar shape + the raw number. Long pale bar across most of the row = cluster firing for ages. Short thick bar near the right edge = same hot week.

bullets.label: bursty (< 5d) → destructive border; weekly (5-9d) → warning
bullets.detail: Bursty = postmortem-now candidate; weekly/bi-weekly = fix the underlying pattern; monthly/infrequent = neutral. Border tone matches the cadence chip; eye reads urgent rows first.

bullets.detail: fingerprint · 90d badge + recurring N (destructive) + orphan N (muted) + N% recur rate + top: N× busiest-cluster size (omitted when 0). The shape of these 5 chips IS the fleet-quality snapshot.

bullets.detail: 'This thing happened N times.' Everything to the right contextualizes — tier / worst severity / representative title / service / team / span bar / days / cadence / mean duration.

sections.title: Three factors with locked weights summing to 100

bullets.label: Runbook coverage (40 pts)
bullets.detail: RUNBOOK_FRESH_DAYS=90 (full 40), RUNBOOK_STALE_DAYS=180 (half credit), expired/missing → 0. Freshest runbook wins when multiple exist for the service.

bullets.label: On-call coverage (35 pts)
bullets.detail: Full credit for team's schedule with no gaps. SCHEDULE_GAP_PENALTY=10 per gap, floored at 0. No schedule → 0.

bullets.label: Recent MTTR (25 pts)
bullets.detail: MTTR_WINDOW_DAYS=30. Avg MTTR ≤ MTTR_TARGET_MINUTES (60m) → full 25. Linear interp 25 → 0 between 60m and MTTR_CEILING_MINUTES (480m). Returns null when no resolved incidents in window.

bullets.label: Absent MTTR data isn't penalized when other signals are present

Rationale: an absence of recent incidents is positive, not a missing data point. Locked by explicit test. Differs from v197 / v214's strict null propagation — different semantics for 'missing' picked deliberately for this composite.

bullets.label: no_data band fires only when ALL three signals are absent
bullets.detail: If service has no runbook AND no schedule AND no incidents-in-window, we can't score and the band is no_data. Otherwise we score with the available signals.

sections.title: Per-anchor incident filtering — the load-bearing trick

bullets.label: Underlying rollup filters by 30d lower bound only
bullets.detail: buildServiceReadinessRollup has no upper bound on incidents — without care, recent incidents would leak into the prior snapshot too. v207 filters incidents PER ANCHOR before running the rollup: current ≤ now; prior ≤ now − 7d. bullets.label: Promoted: largest band-gap first, then most-positive scoreDelta
bullets.detail: at-risk → ready (biggest improvement) sorts before watch → ready.

name: v195 — per-service monitor coverage classification (pulseApmCoverage port from xcl-bff) + MCP tool
intro: Thirteenth xcl-bff port. The BFF's pulseApmCoverage is log-query-bound, but the classifier pattern is portable: a substrate ratio threshold plus a mandatory insufficient_data band that fires before any of the others. Truehound applies the pattern to per-service monitor coverage — answers 'which services are operating without a safety net?' 4 bands: blind (0 monitors) → sparse (under tier expectation) → covered → insufficient_data (no tier). Tier-aware: tier1 ≥ 5, tier2 ≥ 3, tier3 ≥ 1. MCP catalog grows 61 → 62.

sections.title: Verbatim from BFF v1 (the two load-bearing rules)

bullets.label: Ratio threshold below which a service is 'blind'
bullets.detail: BFF: <1% trace_id coverage. Truehound: 0 monitors. The threshold is substrate-adapted but the pattern is identical — a single numerical floor below which the band flips to blind.

bullets.label: MIN_*_TO_DECIDE invariant — refuse to classify when substrate is too thin
bullets.detail: BFF: <1000 logs → don't classify. Truehound: tier missing/unknown → insufficient_data. The band fires BEFORE any of the other three. Locked by an explicit test (100 monitors with no tier still reads as insufficient_data — no ghost math).

bullets.label: SPARSE_THRESHOLD = { tier1: 5, tier2: 3, tier3: 1 }
bullets.detail: Tier1 blast radius is largest → most coverage expected. Tier3 is internal → one monitor is enough. Exported as a Record<tier, number> so consumers and tests pin the contract — updating an expectation is a one-line edit.

bullets.label: classifyMonitorCoverage exported as standalone helper
bullets.detail: Tests pin the rule independently of the rollup. Returns { band, expectedAtLeast } where expectedAtLeast is null on insufficient_data (mirrors v193's 'no number we don't know' discipline).

sections.title: Sort order matches the action priority

bullets.label: blind → sparse → insufficient_data → covered
bullets.detail: insufficient_data sorts AFTER sparse because 'we don't know' is less actionable than a known sparse gap. Within a band, sort by monitorCount ascending (less coverage = worse).

bullets.detail: No registered builder = no way to compare, so trust the caller's intent and return the input. Same as BFF.

sections.title: Rules ported verbatim from BFF v1

bullets.label: Five constants locked
bullets.detail: LOW_SIGNAL_THRESHOLD_COUNT = 5; LOW_SIGNAL_THRESHOLD_RATE = 0.01; MIN_SNAPSHOTS_FOR_COMPARISON = 4; DATA_MATURITY_THRESHOLD = 12 months; TIER_WEIGHT = { tier1: 3, tier2: 2, tier3: 1 }. All exported so consumers and tests pin the contract.

bullets.label: avg, classifyTrend, isLowSignal exported as standalone helpers
bullets.detail: Three small pure functions usable on any time-series; tests verify rules independently of the derivation.

sections.title: Why this is different from the existing weekly strips

bullets.label: Window-vs-window, not raw counts
bullets.detail: v134/v136/v140/v143/v167 show counts per week — useful for spotting spikes. v177 splits monthly snapshots into current half vs previous half, computes deltas, classifies direction-aware (up_good improves on positive delta; down_good improves on negative).

bullets.label: Low-signal gating prevents 0.1% → 0.3% noise
bullets.detail: Counts < 5 or rates < 1% marked isLowSignal: true and excluded from highlights.

bullets.label: Impact scoring = |delta| × tierWeight × dataMaturity
bullets.detail: Tier weights ensure tier-1 moves rank higher; maturity dampens unstable signals from short histories.

bullets.label: Monthly bucketing + per-metric analysis
bullets.detail: Builds 12 (configurable, 1..36) UTC calendar-month snapshots. Per metric: { currentValue, currentWindowAvg, previousWindowAvg, delta, pct, trend, isLowSignal, impactScore }. Top-N improving + degrading highlights sorted by impactScore desc.

bullets.label: Default ATLAS_INCIDENT_METRIC_REGISTRY
bullets.detail: 5 incident KPIs (totalCount tier2, criticalCount tier1, highCount tier2, customerImpactingCount tier1, meanDurationMinutes tier2) — all down_good direction. Custom registries accepted for non-default analyses.

bullets.label: Strict { monthsBack?, highlightLimit? } schema
bullets.detail: monthsBack: 1..36. highlightLimit: 1..20. Pulls 2000 incidents DESC. sensitivity: 'safe', cacheable 60s.

bullets.label: 28 new tests across constants + helpers + derivation
bullets.detail: 5 verbatim-constant tests + 2 avg + 4 classifyTrend + 2 isLowSignal + 15 buildIncidentKpiTrends (default snapshots, bucketing, severity/customer/duration agg, mean-duration finite-only, hasEnoughData, window delta direction-aware, low-signal exclusion, impactScore sort, maturity dampening, custom registry, highlightLimit, default registry shape, monthsBack clamp, future/invalid skip). 1,958 SPA tests total (+28).

bullets.label: Section names mirror the BFF order
bullets.detail: openIncidents → recentlyResolved24h → flappingMonitors24h → expiringSnoozes72h → recentHighTrafficDeploys. The BFF intended these names to be stable for the on-call runbook; Truehound mirrors them so a future BFF wire-up needs to swap fixtures, not the contract.

bullets.label: Per-section sources mapped to Truehound substrate
bullets.detail: openIncidents → Incident.status === 'open'. recentlyResolved24h → resolvedAt within 24h. flappingMonitors24h → noisy && status !== 'muted'. expiringSnoozes72h → mutedUntil ∈ (now, now+72h]. recentHighTrafficDeploys → criticalPath OR speed=Fast OR hasViolation, within 24h.

bullets.label: Per-section sort tuned for action
bullets.detail: Open: severity rank → oldest first. Recently-resolved: most recent first. Flapping: priority asc (1 = urgent). Expiring snoozes: soonest-expiring first. Recent deploys: most recent first.

bullets.label: Three statistics per team: mean / median / p90
bullets.detail: Mean drives the band. Median is the typical case. p90 surfaces tail risk — the slowest 10% often is the problem. name: v156 — service-deployment-staleness rollup + MCP tool
intro: v156 promotes Service.lastDeployedAt to its own rollup. bullets.detail: The Services table already has the column. But sorted by lastDeployedAt it doesn't tell you which services are tier-1 abandoned (paged when down, hasn't shipped in a year). The rollup combines age + tier + critical-path into the danger flag.

name: v152 — slo-budget-burn-by-team rollup + MCP tool
intro: v152 closes an obvious gap in the per-team stack. bullets.detail: { sloCount, worstBudgetPct, avgBudgetPct (count-weighted), avgBurnRate24h, exhaustedSloCount (< 10%), criticalBurnSloCount (burn > 5×), worstSlo, band }. bullets.detail: burning: any exhausted OR worst burnRate > 5×. at-risk: avgBudget < 25% OR any critical-burn. watch: avgBudget < 50%. healthy: otherwise. Sort: avgBudgetPct asc → exhaustedSloCount desc → team asc.

name: v150 — dependency-cycles detection (Tarjan's SCC) + MCP tool
intro: v150 is algorithmically different from every other v96+ derivation. The stack so far has been counting / averaging / banding over flat record sets. v150 is graph theory — Tarjan's strongly-connected-components over service dependency edges, surfacing real circular-dependency groups. Cycles are real SRE concerns: deployment ordering, cascading failures, latency amplification. MCP catalog grows 40 → 41.

bullets.label: Tarjan's SCC, implemented iteratively
bullets.detail: Explicit callStack of frames avoids blowing the JS call stack on deep graphs. Each strongly-connected component of size > 1 is a cycle; size-1 SCCs are cycles only if they have a self-loop. Per-cycle: { id, members, size, hasCriticalEdge, kinds, internalEdgeCount }.

bullets.label: hasCriticalEdge is the most dangerous bit
bullets.detail: True iff any edge inside the cycle is critical: true. Critical-edge cycle = failure on either side pages, recovery loop is closed. Sort: hasCriticalEdge desc → size desc → id asc. Critical cycles surface first regardless of size.

bullets.label: kinds union surfaces deployable-as-async vs. sync-bug
bullets.detail: Sorted union of sync/async/data edges in the cycle. Pure-async cycle is usually fine; sync cycle is usually a bug. Bands: safe (0), noted (1-2 soft), entangled (3+ cycles OR any critical edge).

sections.title: Fresh shape — graph theory, not aggregation

bullets.detail: v138 answers 'who depends on this?' (fan-in count). v150 answers 'are there closed loops?' (graph topology). Same data, different lens. The v96+ stack now spans posture / coverage / fan-in / time-series / financial / human / meta-composite / graph-theory.

intro: v142 breaks the substrate-then-UI rhythm intentionally. After 21 paired ships in the v96+ arc, v142 ships pure UI consolidation: a new /health route that lifts the three time-series triad strips + the two flagship per-team composites onto one screen, then links back to the deep-dive pages for everything else. First purely UI ship in the v96+ arc — no new derivation, no new MCP tool — and it earns its place as the climax of the triad.

name: v29 — Loop trend sparkline + failure retraction + BFF-mode MCP + public tile
intro: v29 closes four small but load-bearing gaps in the loop substrate: a trend sparkline on /briefing so a team sees their SLO trajectory, not just today's number; a failure path on the action store that withdraws v24's implicit feedback when the action fails; an MCP tool that pulls real BFF data instead of synthetic when wired; and the public landing page finally names the loop as a capability.

bullets.detail: Pure SVG, tone-aware (success below SLO, warning above), dashed threshold line at 24h, gaps drawn as pen-lifts. Quiet when <2 populated samples. Renders between description + bucket bars in LoopVelocityCard.

bullets.label: actionStore.markFailed
bullets.detail: New entry point transitions an action to 'failed' and WITHDRAWS the v24 implicit useful vote for each linked signal whose note matches the 'Implicit vote from action <id> (executed)' prefix. Explicit operator votes preserved.

bullets.label: query_loop_health swaps to real BFF data
bullets.detail: When ATLAS_BFF_URL is set, fans out to /api/v1/loop-velocity + /history in parallel. Tolerant shape extractor; graceful 404/network/abort fallback to synthetic. Only velocity swaps; pulse_actions / feedback / top_learning_categories stay synthetic.

bullets.label: /welcome 'Self-learning loop' tile
bullets.detail: Fifth capability tile on the public landing page (Activity icon, links to /pulse). Same visual weight as the other four. Page stays calm — no pricing, no scroll, no comparison.

README + ARCHITECTURE.md + the MCP spec now name the v23-v27 loop as a core capability.

name: v26 — Loop substrate across 5 runtimes
intro: v26 surfaces the v23-v25 loop across every runtime Truehound ships to. The BFF returns action counts on each persistent signal; a new MCP read tool gives agents the action history; the SPA gets self-learning health + loop-velocity cards on /briefing plus a Cause filter on /actions; the Backstage plugin renders the action history on entity cards; the Slack relay handles pulse.signal_opened with severity-emoji formatting. New architecture spec captures the whole loop in one document.

name: v25 — Action history per signature + Recently-learned footer
intro: v25 makes the v23/v24 loop visible. Every persistent Pulse signal row now shows the actions Truehound has already filed against this exact (service, signature), and the page footer shows how the calibrator is learning — explicit operator clicks vs. v24's implicit action-derived votes.

bullets.label: buildActionHistoryForSignature derivation
bullets.detail: Filters the action store to pulse-cause actions matching (service, signature). Each entry carries an implicitFeedbackWritten flag so the surface highlights the ones that actually wrote a learning vote on execute.

bullets.label: ActionHistoryDisclosure on /pulse persistent rows
bullets.detail: Collapsed by default; header shows count + executed count + 'N learned' badge. Expands to per-action rows with proposer, status, reason, and 'Implicit useful vote recorded on execute' footnote.

bullets.label: Distinguishes explicit from implicit votes
bullets.detail: buildRecentlyLearned tags each entry by note prefix — v24's implicit votes have a stable 'Implicit vote from action <id> (executed)' format. Explicit clicks fall back to the explicit chip.

bullets.label: Headline tally on /pulse footer
bullets.detail: 'N explicit · M from action (P%)' — the % from action is the self-learning thesis in a number. Rises over time when Truehound is tuning from outcomes, stays at 0 when the loop isn't closing in production.

bullets.label: 7 new derivation tests
bullets.detail: actionHistoryForSignature (service+sig filter, sort, implicit flag, empty shape) + recentlyLearned (sort, source detection, full-set totals).

name: v24 — Inverse direction of the action loop + Backstage deep-link
intro: v24 closes the inverse direction of v23: a pulse-cause CorrectiveAction reaching `executed` writes an implicit `useful` vote to pulseFeedback for each linked signature. The self-learning Pulse calibrator now tunes from outcomes, not just operator clicks. Plus a Backstage deep-link so the v23 motion is reachable from a third surface.

bullets.label: actionStore.execute() writes feedback for pulse causes
bullets.detail: For each linkedSignals[i], marks the signature as 'useful' with the approver as actor + execution completion time as at. Free-text note records the originating action id.

bullets.label: No-op for non-pulse causes + empty linkedSignals
bullets.detail: Substrate change only — the feedback loop is opt-in by virtue of cause discriminator + linkedSignals presence. Drift / insight / manual actions don't touch pulseFeedback.

bullets.label: Calibrator now learns from action, not just clicks
bullets.detail: Before v24, an operator who took action on a signal but never clicked thumbs was invisible to learning. Taking action is the strongest 'useful' vote — v24 records it automatically.

bullets.label: PulseSignalsCard rows link to /pulse?signature=<sig>
bullets.detail: Only on open + degraded statuses; resolved rows don't surface the link. Reachable from the Backstage entity overview without leaving the catalog.

bullets.label: Truehound /pulse focuses the matching row
bullets.detail: useSearchParams() reads `signature`; the matching PersistentRow gets a ring-2 ring-primary highlight + smooth scrollIntoView. Works for any deep-link source — Backstage, Slack, agent follow-ups.

bullets.label: 3 new actions tests
bullets.detail: Writes feedback for pulse-cause executed, ignores non-pulse causes, ignores empty linkedSignals.

bullets.label: 895 tests total
bullets.detail: 601 SPA + 216 BFF + 49 MCP + 21 Backstage + 8 Slack-relay. lint + typecheck + build green.

name: v23 — Pulse → action proposal loop
intro: v23 closes the most-asked-about loop in the demo: a persistent Pulse signal is now one click away from a CorrectiveAction that travels the same two-key approval rail the dispute-loop already uses. The audit chain records the *signal* — not just the timestamp — as proximate cause. MCP agents propose the same shape through the same envelope.

bullets.label: CorrectiveAction.cause.kind: 'pulse'
bullets.detail: Type extension on src/data/truth/types.ts. cause.id is the signal signature; linkedSignals[] carries the captured snapshot so the audit names which signature the proposer reacted to.

bullets.label: ProposeActionFromSignal CTA
bullets.detail: On /pulse, every open/degraded persistent signal grows a 'Propose action' button. Routes through actionStore.propose with risk=reversible, cause={kind:'pulse',id:signature}. Collapses to 'Action in flight' chip when one is already open against the same (service, signature).

bullets.label: Idempotency via cause.id
bullets.detail: actionStore.hasOpenFor(service, signature) catches duplicates without a separate lookup table — the cause discriminator does double-duty.

bullets.label: Input schema gains linked_signals[]
bullets.detail: Optional array of { signature, service, severity, category, last_detected_at, description }. Server filters out malformed entries (missing signature or service).

bullets.label: Envelope surfaces the proximate cause
bullets.detail: When supplied, the response's _truth_layer.linked_signals echoes the validated array. Agents like Resolve AI / Komodor Klaudia / DD Bits can hand humans a targeted proposal instead of an opaque intent string.

bullets.label: IncidentSignalsAttachment links forward
bullets.detail: When the incident has a postmortem, the 7-day pre-page disclosure surfaces a link to the postmortem's 14-day window. Reachable from the live incident write-up.

bullets.label: PostmortemSignalsAttachment links back
bullets.detail: Every postmortem card surfaces a link to the triggering incident's pre-page window. An auditor sees both windows without hunting.

bullets.label: Inline disclosure per postmortem card
bullets.detail: Lookback window 14d before publishedAt; one row per signal with severity, category, relative time.

bullets.label: Copy as Markdown
bullets.detail: Pre-formatted table with pipe-escaped descriptions, header naming source semantics for the auditor.

name: Pulse v19 — SPA mirror + audit-replay endpoint
intro: Two legs close the v18 substrate loop on the SPA side and expose the chain for postmortem attachment. When VITE_BFF_URL is set, /pulse mirrors feedback to the BFF and hydrates on mount; a small 'shared' badge surfaces the cross-user state. And a new audit-replay endpoint returns the chained pulse.signal_opened events for a service — procurement-grade evidence for postmortems.

bullets.label: Hydrates from BFF on first mount
bullets.detail: Local wins on signalId collisions — operator's fresh click beats a stale server page.

bullets.label: Mirrors every local write
bullets.detail: Fire-and-forget POST /api/v1/pulse/feedback; failures log, never block. Demo mode (no VITE_BFF_URL) behaves identically to v18.

bullets.detail: Operator sees when feedback is converging cross-user vs per-browser.

bullets.label: Returns chained pulse.signal_opened events
bullets.detail: From the v18 pulse-sweep. Optional ?service=<name> + ?since=<iso> filters.

bullets.label: Procurement-grade chain order preserved

name: Pulse v18 — BFF feedback persistence + sweep + audit chain
intro: Two legs promote Pulse from a per-browser localStorage feature to a tenant-shared, procurement-grade substrate. Operator feedback now persists on the BFF (calibration converges across users). And a new pulse-sweep emits webhooks + appends hash-chained audit events whenever a signature newly opens — persistent signals are now evidence-grade alongside action.executed.

bullets.label: pulse-feedback is a first-class KIND
bullets.detail: POST /api/v1/pulse/feedback accepts single or batch; upserts by signalId. GET returns the page for analytics.

bullets.label: Calibration reads persisted feedback by default
bullets.detail: /api/v1/admin/pulse-calibration merges persisted + inline; response carries feedbackSources: { persisted, inline, merged }.

bullets.label: Calibration converges across users in a tenant
bullets.detail: One operator marking useful is visible to the next operator who opens /pulse — no more per-browser drift.

bullets.label: runPulseSweep() parallels confidence-sweep
bullets.detail: Hour-bucketed snapshots, diff against prior, emit pulse.signal_opened + appendAudit for each newly-appearing signature.

bullets.label: pulse-snapshots is a KIND too
bullets.detail: 7-day retention by default; idempotent under retries; POST /api/v1/admin/pulse-sweep exposes manual triggering.

bullets.label: Persistent signals are now procurement-grade
bullets.detail: Same hash-chained audit contract as action.executed — auditors can re-verify offline and see exactly the signal events the platform team saw.

name: Pulse v17 — BFF calibration + anonymized aggregate
intro: Two legs extend self-learning Pulse beyond the SPA's localStorage. The BFF applies the same severity step-down the SPA chip shows, via a forwarded X-Atlas-Calibration header — MCP reads now see the substrate the UI sees. And a new opt-in admin endpoint returns cross-tenant anonymized calibration aggregates with everything identifying stripped.

bullets.label: applyCalibration + parseCalibrationHeader on BFF
bullets.detail: Server-side port; bounded ±1 rung at the scale ends. Endpoint accepts raw or base64-JSON via X-Atlas-Calibration. Tuned rows carry calibrationApplied + note.

bullets.label: SPA window provider
bullets.detail: signalCalibration exposes getCurrentCalibration + window.__atlasCalibration so httpRepository forwards the header without coupling to React. Same pattern as v7 action-state hand-off.

bullets.label: MCP reads now see the same severity the chip shows
bullets.detail: An agent reading /pulse/persistent with the calibration attached gets the operator-tuned severity, not the rule-assigned one. 7 new BFF tests pin the math + header parsing.

bullets.label: POST /api/v1/admin/pulse-calibration/anonymized
bullets.detail: Returns per-category totals + rates + verdicts. No tenant id, actor names, service names, or notes — only the aggregate.

bullets.label: Opt-in required
bullets.detail: X-Atlas-Opt-In-Anonymized-Share: true required; 403 without. Schema version atlas/calibration-anonymized/v1.

bullets.label: Why
bullets.detail: Lets Truehound see which rules trend noisy across the install base without exfiltrating tenant identity. Privacy-respecting analytics surface.

name: Pulse v16 — MCP query tool + calibration-drift card
intro: Two legs round out the loop with the visible time dimension. The MCP server gained an 8th read tool — query_pulse_signals — so agents can read persistent failure patterns directly. And /briefing grew a calibration-drift card that names whether each category's verdict is stable, converging, oscillating, or too new to call.

bullets.label: Calls the v15 BFF endpoint
bullets.detail: Optional service + status filters mirror the BFF API. No required fields — agents can ask 'what patterns are open right now' without prior context.

bullets.label: Same _truth_layer envelope
bullets.detail: freshness + confidence + audit_chain_ref ride along like every other read tool. 2 new MCP tests; tools/list at 9 (8 read + propose).

bullets.label: Daily snapshot store
bullets.detail: localStorage + BroadcastChannel; one snapshot per ISO date, auto-trimmed to 60 days. Side-effect hook on /briefing records once per render — no new operator action.

bullets.label: Four-state drift verdict
bullets.detail: stable / converging (two labels — settling) / oscillating (≥3 labels — rule still being figured out) / new (≤2 samples). 8 SPA tests pin the math.

bullets.label: Per-category sparkline on /briefing
bullets.detail: Inline mini-chart + drift chip + latest rate. Platform teams see whether feedback is converging or oscillating across categories.

The BFF gained /api/v1/pulse/persistent (writer pipeline materializes dedup, not every read client). The Backstage plugin gained PulseSignalsCard that reads from it — entity overview pages now surface persistent failure patterns alongside ownership confidence.

bullets.detail: Port of buildPersistentSignals — open/degraded/resolved status, severity-max escalation. ?service= + ?status= filters. OpenAPI documented.

bullets.detail: Raw signals join services/incidents/monitors in the BFF persistence layer. 10 parity tests assert identical outputs to the SPA derivation.

bullets.detail: Severity + category chips, description, detection count, last-seen relative time. Quiet by default — renders nothing when no signals or older BFF (avoids clutter).

bullets.detail: 5 new plugin tests: URL shape, 404 fallback, 5xx surfacing, status filter, empty-name guard. Plugin at 0.3.0 → 0.4.0.

name: Pulse v14 — persistent signals + webhook + calibration export
intro: Three legs round out v13 by porting the xcl-tools persistent-signals contract and reusing the v10 Slack relay for Pulse events. Truehound's /pulse page now toggles between raw detections and persistent (signature-grouped) records. A new pulse.signal_opened webhook routes through the existing relay substrate. And an admin endpoint exports per-tenant calibration verdicts as JSON for analytics dashboards.

bullets.label: Raw / Persistent toggle on /pulse
